Module 1.title: Single Variable Calculus and Infinite Series
Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Calculus & Series
  • Rolle's & Mean Value Theorems: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$, $\exists c \in (a,b)$ such that $f'(c) = \frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$.
  • Taylor & Maclaurin Series: $f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!} (x - a)^n$.
  • Series Convergence Tests: Ratio test ($\lim |a_{n+1}/a_n| < 1$), Integral test, Alternating series Leibniz test.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Module 1 Reference: Calculus

Indeterminate forms evaluated using L'Hôpital's rule.
Module 1.textbook_html:

Module 2.title: Multivariable Differential Calculus and Optimization
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Multivariable Calculus
  • Partial Derivatives: Euler's theorem for homogeneous functions of degree $n$: $x u_x + y u_y = n u$.
  • Jacobian: $J = \frac{\partial(u,v)}{\partial(x,y)} = u_x v_y - u_y v_x$.
  • Maxima & Minima of Two Variables: $r = f_{xx}, s = f_{xy}, t = f_{yy}$. If $rt - s^2 > 0$ and $r < 0$ (Local Maxima); if $rt - s^2 > 0$ and $r > 0$ (Local Minima); if $rt - s^2 < 0$ (Saddle point).
  • Lagrange Multipliers: $\nabla f = \lambda \nabla g$ for constrained optimization.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Module 2 Reference: Multivariable

Gradient vector $\nabla f$ points in the direction of maximum directional rate of increase.

Module 3.title: Multiple Integrals and Coordinate Transformations
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Double & Triple Integrals
  • Change of Variables (Cartesian to Polar): $dx dy = r dr d\theta$.
  • Area via Double Integration: $A = \iint_R dx dy = \iint_R r dr d\theta$.
  • Volume via Triple Integration: $V = \iiint_V dx dy dz$. In cylindrical coordinates: $r dr d\theta dz$. In spherical coordinates: $\rho^2 \sin \phi d\rho d\phi d\theta$.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Multiple Integrals

Beta and Gamma functions: $\Gamma(n) = \int_0^\infty x^{n-1} e^{-x} dx$. $\Gamma(1/2) = \sqrt{\pi}$.

Module 4.title: Vector Differential and Integral Calculus (Green, Stokes, Gauss)
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Vector Theorems
  • Gradient, Divergence & Curl: $ ext{grad } \phi = abla \phi$, $ ext{div } \vec{F} = abla \cdot \vec{F}$, $ ext{curl } \vec{F} = abla imes \vec{F}$. Irrotational field: $ abla imes \vec{F} = 0$. Solenoidal field: $ abla \cdot \vec{F} = 0$.
  • Green's Theorem in Plane: $\oint_C (M dx + N dy) = \iint_R \left( rac{\partial N}{\partial x} - rac{\partial M}{\partial y} ight) dx dy$.
  • Stokes' Theorem: $\oint_C \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = \iint_S ( abla imes \vec{F}) \cdot \hat{n} dS$.
  • Gauss Divergence Theorem: $\iint_S \vec{F} \cdot \hat{n} dS = \iiint_V ( abla \cdot \vec{F}) dV$.

Module 5.title: Linear Algebra: Matrices, Eigenvalues and Diagonalization
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Matrices & Eigenvalues
  • Rank of Matrix: Number of non-zero rows in row-echelon form. System $A X = B$ is consistent iff $\text{rank}(A) = \text{rank}(A|B)$.
  • Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors: Characteristic equation $|A - \lambda I| = 0$. Sum of eigenvalues equals Trace($A$); Product of eigenvalues equals $\det(A)$.
  • Cayley-Hamilton Theorem: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation: $A^n + c_{n-1}A^{n-1} + \dots + c_0 I = 0$. Used to compute $A^{-1}$ and high powers $A^m$.
  • Diagonalization: If $A$ has $n$ linearly independent eigenvectors, $P^{-1} A P = D$ (diagonal matrix of eigenvalues).

Module 5 Reference: Linear Algebra
